title: GPU node-pool Terraform module with canary upgrades and health-probe hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU-backed node groups inside customer VPCs with two operating modes: managed ASG (for stable capacity and lifecycle control) and Karpenter (for bursty/spot-friendly workloads). The module must support canary/rolling upgrades, health-probe hooks that validate GPU driver and CUDA readiness, and safe fallback to ASG on Karpenter capacity failures. Deliverables: 1) Terraform module (inputs/outputs documented), 2) upgrade strategy implementation (canary policy + automated health gating), 3) end-to-end tests and CI pipeline, 4) example usage for Private control plane and on-prem air-gapped variant.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module provisions GPU node groups (ASG and Karpenter) in a customer VPC with configurable instance types and AMI
Canary upgrade path that replaces <=10% of nodes first and runs GPU readiness checks before continuing
Health-probe Lambda or DaemonSet that verifies NVIDIA driver, nvidia-smi, and model-serving readiness on each node
Karpenter fallback policy: if Karpenter cannot fulfill GPU requests for >2m, route new capacity to ASG fallback pool
Module exports outputs useful for Console (autoscaler_group_id, karpenter_provisioner_name, nodepool_version)
E2E test that simulates a bad AMI and demonstrates automatic rollback via canary gating
Documented Terraform variables and migration notes for existing customers using legacy gpu-nodegroup module
implementation_notes: Key design decisions: 1) Use a single module with 'mode' var: 'asg' | 'karpenter' | 'hybrid' to avoid duplicate modules; 2) Upgrade strategy implemented using lifecycle hooks for ASG + Karpenter provisioner rollingForces and a controller that annotates nodes for safe drain; 3) Health probe implemented as a DaemonSet (primary) with a Lambda fallback that scrapes node annotations for cluster-admin telemetry; 4) GPU readiness = driver loaded AND nvidia-smi returns expected CUDA version AND test inference container starts and returns 200 inside 30s; 5) Support mixed instance types (g5/g4d/p4) with weight-based capacity mapping and on-failure migration policy.
terraform_examples: # To trigger a canary upgrade, bump module var nodepool_version and run 'terraform apply'
runbook_steps: 1. Review plan output and ensure canary nodes count = ceil(desired_capacity * canary_percentage / 100)
2. Apply terraform (CI triggers deploy pipeline that creates new ASG launch template or updates Karpenter provisioner)
3. Monitor health-probe DaemonSet logs in cluster and Console 'nodepool' dashboard
4. If canary probes fail: abort by reverting Terraform change or run 'terraform taint' on canary instances and roll back AMI to previous knit
5. After canary succeeds, continue rollout. If rollout stalls >15m, open P0 incident and run fallback script 'scripts/force-asg-fallback.sh'
6. Post-mortem: capture failing node logs, GPU driver diagnostics, and store under Drive > Private Deployments > GPU-upgrade-YYYYMMDD
test_plan: Unit: validate Terraform variable validation and plan-only CI job
Integration: spin up a small test cluster in sandbox VPC (2 GPUs), run canary upgrade with a bad AMI to ensure gating triggers rollback
Chaos: simulate Karpenter API failures and assert ASG fallback activates within 2m
Performance: run 1h load test to measure pod launch latency for cold vs cached images with Karpenter vs ASG
Security: verify tags/iam roles are least-privilege for private control plane and KMS access for AMI secrets
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Karpenter may schedule GPUs onto instance types our AMI doesn't support -> Mitigation: validate AMI image-builder across all instance families and add admission webhook to reject unsupported types
Risk: Canary gating too strict and blocks upgrades -> Mitigation: provide operator override with audit logging and require two approvals for bypass
Risk: Draining GPU nodes affects long-running model downloads -> Mitigation: use cordon+drain with PodDisruptionBudget awareness and pre-copy model caches to new nodes
Risk: Private/on-prem air-gapped variant can't fetch drivers -> Mitigation: provide offline driver bundle and a validation script that runs during AMI bake
